title: An Effective String Theory Toolbox for Quantum Hall Interfaces III: Open Worldsheets, Endpoint Conditions, and Branes
abstract: A freely moving quantum Hall (QH) interface may end on a physical edge or topological boundary, but fixed-edge theory cannot determine what endpoint data make such a termination consistent. Here we formulate an open-worldsheet junction framework in which the embedding, material charge, anomaly flow, and topological boundary condition are organized together. The endpoint is specified by a geometric support and variational boundary data, together with condensable topological sectors and any outgoing channels required to absorb or continue the worldsheet flux. This construction extends the charge--shape relation to an interval and shows why a lone chiral Majorana cannot terminate on a finite-dimensional endpoint degree of freedom. It gives an operational definition of a QH brane and a systematic basis for endpoint and network theories of dynamical QH interfaces.
summary: This paper develops an advanced string theory toolbox to handle the complex physics of mobile Quantum Hall (QH) interfaces that terminate at edges. It constructs a junction framework that rigorously enforces charge and anomaly conservation across these boundaries. The result provides a systematic, operational definition for QH branes and endpoint theories.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a consistent theoretical framework for determining the endpoint data required for a freely moving Quantum Hall (QH) interface that terminates on a physical or topological boundary.
main_result: The authors establish an open-worldsheet junction framework, showing that charge conservation and anomaly flow dictate that specific localized excitations, like a lone chiral Majorana, cannot terminate without satisfying complex continuity conditions.
method: The work employs variational principles applied to the worldsheet action, developing specialized boundary functionals (like the capped relative-area functional) to enforce consistency across geometric, material, and topological sectors.
model_or_system: The model is a mobile QH interface treated as an open worldsheet embedded in a background manifold. It incorporates concepts from string theory, chiral edge states, and topological order relevant to fractional quantum Hall physics.
key_observables: Endpoint force (F), bending moment (M), material charge ($Q_{mat}$), total charged-boson zero mode ($Q_{seg}$), and the scattering matrix $S_\gamma(\omega)$.

main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to fixed open segments; processes involving worldsheet splitting or joining are considered beyond the scope of this specific construction.

paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing mechanical boundary terms via variational calculus to formulating the junction framework. It then details charge conservation laws, analyzes endpoint completion using topological sectors (open Wilson lines), and concludes with specific scattering analyses for Majorana junctions.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, field-theoretic approach to open quantum systems boundaries, which is highly relevant for understanding dissipation, coupling to leads, or interfaces in condensed matter systems like superconducting qubits or topological insulators.
